reason: The text portrays the conflict primarily as a religious and cosmic struggle under divine direction, not as a political fight for liberty. The battle's outcome is explicitly dependent on supernatural elements: Moses's rod (described as 'the rod of God') and God's direct control—when Moses raises his hand, Israel prevails; when lowered, Amalek prevails. God commands Moses to record this as a memorial and promises to 'utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.' The passage concludes by explicitly framing this as 'the LORD's war against Amalek from generation to generation' (מִלְחָמָה לַיהוָה בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר), emphasizing cosmic, eternal conflict rather than political autonomy. Moses builds an altar calling God 'my banner,' further emphasizing the religious character. The Hebrews' military action is subordinate to and dependent upon divine intervention, not autonomous political agency.
